Millions of Toothpaste Tubes Recalled Nationwide: What Parents Need to Know

31 Oct 2026, 05:13 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Lifestyle Desk · Source: www.nbcnews.com

More than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste, including popular children's brands featuring kid-themed flavors like bubble gum, strawberry, and watermelon, have been voluntarily recalled nationwide following manufacturing issues flagged by federal regulators.

The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced the nationwide recall after discovering current good manufacturing practice deviations at the facility that produced the items. While the affected products could still be sitting in medicine cabinets with expiration dates stretching as far out as mid-2028, officials have confirmed that no injuries or illnesses have been reported in connection with the recall.

Understanding the Recall and Affected Brands

The voluntary recall was initiated on September 10 by Pritam International Private Limited, a manufacturer based in India, and was officially classified by the FDA as a Class II recall on October 19. A Class II designation applies to products that may cause temporary or medically reversible health issues, where the likelihood of serious adverse effects remains low.

The affected inventory includes several well-known brands distributed by Ashtel Studios Inc., based in Ontario, California. Recalled products were sold under brand names such as Brush Buddies, Crayola, Hot Wheels, and My Little Pony. Available flavors span kids' varieties like bubble gum, strawberry, and watermelon, alongside adult options such as peppermint, sweet mint, and cool mint. The items were packaged in 3.5-ounce and 4-ounce tubes, as well as a two-pack of 3.5-ounce tubes.

Practical Implications and What Readers Should Do

Because expiration dates on the impacted items stretch from November 2026 through June 2028, consumers are urged to review their bathroom supplies.

  • Check Your Products: Inspect the brand name, lot numbers, and expiration dates on your toothpaste tubes and compare them directly against the official FDA recall notice.
  • Discontinue Use: Although no specific return or refund guidance has been formally issued by the manufacturer or distributor, the safest immediate step is to stop using any matching toothpaste and discard it.
  • Retain Documentation: Keep your purchase receipt or snap a photograph of the product packaging before throwing it away in case a formal refund or return process becomes available later.
  • Consult Professionals: While no health issues have been documented, individuals or parents whose children used the recalled items and who harbor health concerns should reach out to a doctor or dentist.

Confirmed Facts Versus Unknowns

  • Confirmed: More than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste distributed by Ashtel Studios and manufactured by Pritam International have been recalled due to manufacturing practice deviations. The FDA classified this as a Class II recall. No illnesses or injuries have been reported.
  • Unknown: Specific consumer instructions regarding returns, refunds, or exchanges have not yet been released by the manufacturer or distributor.

Readers can verify all official details, specific lot numbers, and affected product descriptions directly through the [FDA Official Recall Notice](https://www.nbcnews.com/select/shopping/brush-buddies-evo-toothpaste-recall-2026-rcna605288).
